Having offered an oblation into the fire with "Svaḥ Svāhā," he pours the residue into the mash. Having offered an oblation into the fire with "Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ Svāhā," he pours the residue into the mash. Having offered an oblation into the fire with "Svāhā to Brahman," he pours the residue into the mash. Having offered an oblation into the fire with "Svāhā to Kṣatra," he pours the residue into the mash. Having offered an oblation into the fire with "Svāhā to the Past," he pours the residue into the mash. Having offered an oblation into the fire with "Svāhā to the Future," he pours the residue into the mash. Having offered an oblation into the fire with "Svāhā to All," he pours the residue into the mash. Having offered an oblation into the fire with "Svāhā to the Whole," he pours the residue into the mash. Having offered an oblation into the fire with "Svāhā to Prajāpati," he pours the residue into the mash. (6.3.3)

Then he touches it, saying: "Thou art whirling; thou art flaming; thou art full; thou art rigid; thou art the single assembly; thou art the uttered *hiṅ*; thou art being uttered as *hiṅ*; thou art the *udgītha*; thou art being sung as *udgītha*; thou art the *śrāva*; thou art the *pratyāśrāva*; thou art moist yet kindled; thou art pervasive; thou art powerful; thou art food; thou art light; thou art the finale (*nidhana*); thou art the absorber. (6.3.4)
Then he lifts it up with the formula: "O Āman, great is your greatness; for he is the king, the ruler, the sovereign lord. May he make me the king, the ruler, the sovereign lord. (6.3.5)
Then he sips from it:
"That excellent glory of Savitṛ... "Honeyed are the winds for the one who follows the cosmic order; honeyed streams flow."
May the plants be honey-sweet for us. Bhūḥ Svāhā!
We meditate upon the splendor of the divine.
Honeyed be the night and the dawns; honeyed be the earthly realm.
May the sky be honey for us, our father. Bhuvaḥ! Svāhā! May he who shall impel our thoughts [be so].
May the lord of the forest be full of honey for us; may the sun be full of honey.
"May the cows be honey-sweet for us; heaven, svāhā!

He recites the entire *Sāvitrī* and all the verses containing the word "honey," [thinking] "May I become this whole world; bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā. Finally, having sipped water and washed his hands, he lies down behind the fire with his head toward the east. In the morning, he worships the sun, saying: "Thou art the unique lotus among the quarters; may I become the unique lotus among men. Having returned by the same way he came, sitting behind the fire, he mutters the *vaṃśa*. 6.3.6.
Having told this very same thing to his pupil Vājasaneya Yājñavalkya, Uddālaka Āruṇi said: "Even if one were to pour this upon a withered stump, branches would grow and leaves would sprout."
Vājasaneya Yājñavalkya, having told this very same thing to his pupil Madhuka Paiṅgya, said: "Even if one were to pour this on a withered stump, branches would grow and leaves would sprout."
Madhuka Paiṅgya, having told this very same thing to his pupil Cūla Bhāgavitti, said: "Even if one were to pour it upon a dry stump, branches would grow and leaves would sprout. 6.3.9.

Having said this to Cūla Bhāgavitti, who was a pupil of Āyasthūṇa of the lineage of Janaka, he further declared: "Even if one were to pour water upon a dry stump, branches would grow and leaves would sprout. (6.3.10)
Having told this very thing to his pupil Satyakāma Jābāla, Jānaki Āyasthūṇa said: "Even if one were to pour it onto a dry stump, branches would grow and leaves would sprout. (6.3.11)

Satyakāma Jābāla, having told this very thing to his pupils, said: "Even if one were to pour it onto a withered stump, branches would grow and leaves would sprout. One should not tell this to anyone who is not a son or a pupil. 6.3.12.

There are four items made of *udumbara* wood: a *sruva* ladle of *udumbara*, a *camasa* cup of *udumbara*, a fuel-wood (*idhma*) of *udumbara*, and two churning-sticks (*upamanthanyau*) of *udumbara*. There are ten kinds of cultivated grains: rice, barley, sesame, beans, millet, *priyaṅgu*, wheat, lentils, chickpeas, and *khalakula*. Having ground these, he pours them into curd, honey, and clarified butter; he offers them as an oblation of clarified butter. 6.3.13.
Thus ends the third Brāhmaṇa.
Of these beings, the earth is the essence; of the earth, water; of water, plants; of plants, flowers; of flowers, fruits; of fruits, man; of man, semen. 6.4.1.

Prajāpati reflected: "Come, let me fashion a support for him. He created a woman. Having created her, he approached her from below; therefore, one should approach a woman from below. From his own self, he fashioned this pressing-stone facing eastward; with it, he impregnated her. 6.4.2.

Her altar is her lap; the hair is the sacrificial grass (*barhis*); the skin is the two pressing-boards; the kindled fire is between her thighs, which are the two testicles. As great as is the world of one who performs the *Vājapeya* sacrifice, so great is the world of him who, knowing this, engages in sexual intercourse with these women—he takes away their merit. But he who, not knowing this, engages in sexual intercourse, his women take away his merit. (6.4.3)

Knowing this, Uddālaka Āruṇi indeed said: "Knowing this, Nāka Maudgalya indeed said: 'Many young men of the Brāhmaṇa caste, devoid of power and deprived of merit, depart from this world, they who, not knowing this, engage in sexual intercourse. Indeed, much semen is spilled by one whether sleeping or waking. (6.4.4)
He should touch it, or recite over it:

"That seed of mine which today has fallen upon the earth, which has flowed into the plants, or into the waters—this seed I take back. May my virility return to me; may my splendor return; may my fortune return."
"May Agni and the *dhiṣṇya* fires be established again in their proper places.
Having said this, she should take [the food] with her ring finger and thumb and wipe it between her breasts or her eyebrows. (6.4.5)
Now, if he should see his own reflection in water, he should consecrate it with the mantra: "In me be splendor, sensory power, fame, wealth, and merit."

She who has removed her soiled garment is indeed the very embodiment of glory among women. Therefore, one should approach and address a glorious woman while she is wearing her soiled garment. If she does not yield to him, he may, at his pleasure, purchase her [with gifts]. If she still does not yield to him, he may, at his pleasure, strike her with a stick or with his hand, saying: "I take away your glory with my own manly power and glory. Thus, she becomes indeed devoid of glory. If she should yield to him, he says: "I bestow glory upon you with my own manly power and glory. Thus, both become glorious.
Whichever woman he might desire, thinking, "May she be mine," he should fix his purpose upon her, join mouth to mouth, touch her private parts, and mutter:
"From limb by limb you arise, from the heart you are born; you are the essence of the limbs. Intoxicate this woman for me, as one would intoxicate a poisoned arrow."

Now, if she for whom he desires, "May she not conceive," he should, having performed the ritual purpose with her, join mouth to mouth, breathe in upon her, and then breathe out, saying: "With my organ and my semen, I take away your semen. Thus she becomes indeed seedless. 6.4.10.

Now, if he should desire of a woman, "May she conceive," he should prepare the matter with her, join mouth to mouth, and exhaling and inhaling, say: "With my faculty, with my semen, I place semen in you. She becomes pregnant. 6.4.11.

Now, if one should hate a man who has had an affair with his wife, he should kindle a fire in an unbaked earthen vessel, spread out reed-grass (*śarabarhis*) against the grain, and into that [fire] he should offer these reed-arrows, smeared with clarified butter and pointed against the grain, saying:
"In my kindled fire you have sacrificed; I take back your out-breath and in-breath, O so-and-so! "In my kindled fire you have sacrificed; I take back your sons and cattle, O so-and-so!"
"Into my kindled fire you have sacrificed; I take from you that merit of yours, so-and-so! "Into my kindled fire you have sacrificed; I take from you both your curse and your reward, so-and-so!

He who is cursed by a Brahmin knowing this indeed departs from this world deprived of his senses and stripped of his merit. Therefore, one who knows this should not seek to joke with the wife of a learned Śrotriya, for he who knows this becomes superior. 6.4.12.

Now, if a woman should find her menses, she shall not drink from a bronze vessel for three days; she shall remain in unwashed clothes. Neither a *vṛṣala* nor a *vṛṣalī* woman shall touch her. At the end of the three nights, having bathed, she shall have rice threshed. (6.4.13)

If he should desire, "May a fair son be born to me; may he recite the Veda; may he live his full span of life," they should cook rice with milk and eat it mixed with clarified butter; thus they are capable of procreating [such a son]. 6.4.14.

Now, if one should desire, "May a son be born to me who is tawny and reddish-brown, who may recite two Vedas, and who may live his full lifespan," they should have curd-rice cooked with clarified butter and eat it; thus they will be capable of procreating such a child. 6.4.15.

Now, if one should desire, "May a son be born to me who is dark-complexioned with red eyes, who shall recite the three Vedas and live his full span of life," they should cook rice with milk and eat it with clarified butter; thus they will be capable of procreating such a child. 6.4.16.

Now, if one should desire, "May a wise daughter be born to me, and may she live her full span of life," they should cook rice mixed with sesame seeds and eat it with clarified butter; thus they will be able to procreate such a child. 6.4.17.

Now, if one should desire, "May a son be born to me who is wise, renowned, capable in assembly, a speaker of words that are well-received, who shall master all the Vedas and live his full span of life," they should have meat-rice cooked with clarified butter and eat it; they will thus be able to procreate. [This should be done] with the meat of a bull or a steer. 6.4.18.

Then, at the very break of dawn, having performed the rites with clarified butter according to the procedure for the *sthālīpāka* (cooked-rice offering), he offers a portion of the *sthālīpāka* with the formulas: "To Agni, svāhā! To Anumati, svāhā! To the god Savitṛ of true impulsion, svāhā! Having offered and drawn out [the remainder], he eats it. After eating, he gives the rest to the other [wife]. Having washed his hands and filled a water-vessel, he sprinkles her with that water three times, saying: "Arise from here, O Viśvāvasu; seek another woman who is more favorable. May the wife be united with her husband. || 6.4.19 ||
Then he approaches her, saying:
"I am the *ama*, you are the *sā*; you are the *sā*, I am the *ama*.
I am the *sāman*, you are the *ṛc*; I am heaven, you are the earth."
"Come, let us two be impassioned; let us both deposit seed together, for the sake of obtaining a male son. (6.4.20)

Then he causes her thighs to part, saying: "May you two, Heaven and Earth, open yourselves. Having placed his purpose upon her and joining his mouth to her mouth, he strokes her three times in the direction of the hair with the verse: "May Viṣṇu prepare the womb; may Tvaṣṭṛ fashion the forms;
may Prajāpati pour [the seed]; may Dhātṛ place the embryo within you."
Bestow a fetus, O Sinīvālī; bestow a fetus, O broad-hipped one!
May the two Aśvin gods, wreathed with lotuses, place a fetus within you. 6.4.21.
The two fire-sticks from which the Aśvins churned the golden fire—
through those we invoke this embryo of yours for birth in the tenth month.
"As the earth contains fire within it, as the sky is pregnant with Indra, and as the wind is the embryo of the quarters, so do I place this embryo in you, O [Name]. (6.4.22)
He sprinkles her with water as she is about to give birth:
"As the wind agitates a lotus pond on every side, so may your embryo stir; may it come forth together with the afterbirth."
"This stall has been made for Indra, secured with a bolt and surrounded by a fence;
O Indra, destroy it with your embryo, along with the Sāvarṇas. (6.4.23)

When [the son] has been born, having kindled the fire, having placed him on his lap, and having poured the speckled butter (pṛṣadājya) into a bronze vessel, he offers portions of the speckled butter with the formula:
"In this [son], may I thrive and prosper a thousandfold in my own home;
may he not be cut off from his proximity to me, nor from offspring and cattle."

Svāhā! With my mind, I offer the vital breaths into you; svāhā! Whatever I have done in excess through this rite, or whatever I have done here deficiently—may Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, the wise one, make that well-sacrificed and well-offered for us; svāhā! (6.4.24)

Then, having placed [his hand] over his right ear, he says "Speech! Speech! three times. Then, having mixed together curd, honey, and ghee, he makes him eat it with a piece of gold that is not separated from it, saying: "Bhūḥ, I place in you; Bhuvaḥ, I place in you; Svaḥ, I place in you; Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I place everything in you. (6.4.25)
Then he gives him a name, saying, "You are Veda. That becomes his secret name. (6.4.26) Then, having handed him over to the mother, he gives her the breast, saying:

"That breast of yours which is inexhaustible, which is refreshing, which bestows jewels, which finds wealth, which is a good giver, by which you nourish all desirable things—O Sarasvatī, bring that here for him to suck. (6.4.27)
Then he addresses his mother:
"Thou art Ilā, daughter of Mitra and Varuṇa; thou hast given birth to a hero among heroes.
Mayest thou be rich in heroes, she who has made us rich in heroes."

Regarding him, they say: "Truly you have become a father again; truly you have become a grandfather again! You have indeed reached the highest pinnacle in prosperity, fame, and Vedic splendor, since a son has been born to a Brāhmaṇa who knows this. (6.4.28)
Thus ends the fourth Brāhmaṇa.

Now, the lineage (*vaṃśa*). Pautimāṣīputra from Kātyāyanīputra; Kātyāyanīputra from Gautamīputra; Gautamīputra from Bhāradvājīputra; Bhāradvājīputra from Pārāśarīputra; Pārāśarīputra from Aupasvastīputra; Aupasvastīputra from Pārāśarīputra; Pārāśarīputra from Kātyāyanīputra; Kātyāyanīputra from Kauśikīputra; Kauśikīputra from Ālambīputra and Vaiyāghrapadīputra; Vaiyāghrapadīputra from Kāṇvīputra and Kāpīputra; Kāpīputra from Ātreyīputra; Ātreyīputra from Gautamīputra; Gautamīputra from Bhāradvājīputra; Bhāradvājīputra from Pārāśarīputra; Pārāśarīputra from Vātsīputra; Vātsīputra from Pārāśarīputra; Pārāśarīputra from Vārkāruṇīputra; Vārkāruṇīputra from Vārkāruṇīputra; Vārkāruṇīputra from Ārtabhāgīputra; Ārtabhāgīputra from Śauṅgīputra; Śauṅgīputra from Sāṃkṛtīputra; Sāṃkṛtīputra from Ālambāyanīputra; Ālambāyanīputra from Ālambīputra; Ālambīputra from Jāyantīputra; Jāyantīputra from Māṇḍūkāyanīputra; Māṇḍūkāyanīputra from Māṇḍūkīputra; Māṇḍūkīputra from Śāṇḍilīputra; Śāṇḍilīputra from Rāthītarīputra; Rāthītarīputra from Bhālukīputra; Bhālukīputra from two Krauñcikīputras; the two Krauñcikīputras from Vaidabhṛtīputra; Vaidabhṛtīputra from Kārśakeyīputra; Kārśakeyīputra from Prācīnayogīputra; Prācīnayogīputra from Sāñjīvīputra; Sāñjīvīputra from Prāśnīputra Āsurivāsina; Prāśnīputra from Āsurāyaṇa; Āsurāyaṇa from Āsuri; Āsuri from Yājñavalkya; Yājñavalkya from Uddālaka; Uddālaka from Aruṇa; Aruṇa from Upaveśi; Upaveśi from Kuśri; Kuśri from Vājaśravas; Vājaśravas from Jihvāvān Bādhyoga; Jihvāvān Bādhyoga from Asita Vārṣagaṇa; Asita Vārṣagaṇa from Harita Kaśyapa; Harita Kaśyapa from Śilpa Kaśyapa; Śilpa Kaśyapa from Kaśyapa Naidhruvi; Kaśyapa Naidhruvi from Vāc; Vāc from Ambhiṇī; Ambhiṇī from Āditya. These white *yajus* formulas are proclaimed by Yājñavalkya Vājasaneya, who descended from Āditya. [The lineage] is the same up to Sāñjīvīputra. Sāñjīvīputra from Māṇḍūkāyani; Māṇḍūkāyani from Māṇḍavya; Māṇḍavya from Kautsa; Kautsa from Māhitthi; Māhitthi from Vāmakakṣāyaṇa; Vāmakakṣāyaṇa from Śāṇḍilya; Śāṇḍilya from Vātsya; Vātsya from Kuśri; Kuśri from Yajñavacas Rājastambāyana; Yajñavacas Rājastambāyana from Tura Kāvaṣeya; Tura Kāvaṣeya from Prajāpati; Prajāpati from Brahman. Brahman is self-existent (*svayaṃbhu*). Salutation to Brahman! 6.5.4.1–4.108 (End)
Thus ends the fifth Brāhmaṇa.
Thus ends the sixth chapter.
Thus ends the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad.
